subject.title: [Feature]: Support sessionKey-based concurrency guard for webhook       deliveries

question: Should same-session hook-agent deliveries be rejected with 409, queued or serialized, or remain parallel by default, and should that policy be opt-in per direct hook and mapping?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the choice changes public HTTP retry semantics, session-state behavior, and security-sensitive hook routing, so automation should not choose the API contract.

options.title: Add explicit overlap policy
options.body: Preserve current parallel async behavior by default and add a configured per-hook policy such as reject, queue, or parallel for trusted integrations.

options.title: Fold into queued webhooks
options.body: Let the broader queued-webhook design own burst handling, backlog visibility, and concurrency controls before closing this narrower request.

options.title: Fail closed by default
options.body: Return 409 for overlapping same-session deliveries by default and intentionally accept the compatibility cost for existing async webhook callers.

recommendation.title: Add explicit overlap policy
recommendation.body: Preserve current parallel async behavior by default and add a configured per-hook policy such as reject, queue, or parallel for trusted integrations.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice is a Gateway product/security policy decision, and prior related review comments route this exact decision through steipete.
